name: NIDS - Network Intrusion Detection System
description: Machine learning-based NIDS using CICIDS2017 dataset. Detects DDoS, Port Scans, Brute Force, and Botnet traffic via binary and multiclass flow-level classification with RF/XGBoost and an optional Autoencoder anomaly detector. Includes Streamlit dashboard.
conventions: All scripts accept CLI args via argparse or are importable as modules
Models saved under models/ as .joblib files
Processed data saved under data/processed/ as .parquet files
Logging via Python logging module, not print statements
Every public function has a numpy-style docstring
architecture_patterns: Pipeline pattern: raw CSVs -> preprocessing -> feature engineering -> model training -> evaluation
Binary detection first, then multiclass extension
Offline/batch mode primary; live inference as stretch goal

file_structure.tests: Unit tests for preprocessing and model pipeline

patterns: Unit tests for all preprocessing functions
Integration tests for the full train pipeline

never_do: Never use random shuffle for train/test split — always split by time/day
Never leak test data into preprocessing or scaling fit
Never commit raw data CSVs to git (add to .gitignore)
Never use accuracy alone as the evaluation metric
Never hardcode file paths — use config or argparse
preferred_patterns: Use sklearn Pipeline objects to chain preprocessing + model
Use SMOTE only on training data, never on test data
Use class_weight='balanced' as baseline before SMOTE
Use time-based split to avoid temporal leakage
Use SHAP for all model explanations
sprint_focus: Phase 1-5: Build complete NIDS pipeline from data loading to trained model evaluation
